chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated this hadith from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Ahwal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): like the first one.

The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: When the time for zakat arrives and the deserving recipient is not available with him, he should set it aside from the total of his wealth until he finds someone deserving of it.
ai.seo_question: What should one do with zakat if the deserving recipient is not available when the time for payment arrives?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi highlights this ruling to address the practical scenario where a specific designated recipient (mustahiqq) is absent when zakat becomes due, emphasizing the necessity of segregation (‘azl) to preserve the sanctity of the funds. This ensures the obligation is not discharged prematurely or incorrectly, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of maintaining the specific status of zakat wealth until it reaches its rightful owner.
